notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #12
notes.notes:
Ahoy!

In today’s devlog, we want to show you a bit of the world we’ve designed for the game—one that you’ll be able to explore with your crew and your ship. Keep in mind, though, that the places you visit might hide valuable treasures, but they also come with dangers. Sometimes, you’ll run into trouble, like the Trade Company trying to stop you.

In this post, we’ll give you a closer look at a few interesting locations you can visit on the map—and what you might expect to find there.

[h3]The Quiet Shores – Fishing Village[/h3]

[i]"Aye, the fish be fresh an’ the winds be calm... but don’t expect more than a dry biscuit and a silent stare." — Old Red Flit, sailor and lover of quiet ports[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/253db89a28f61dcbb902bca2c3befc3d8cc86cee.jpg[/img]

One of the locations you can visit is a peaceful fishing village. This small settlement offers basic supplies—most importantly, food, which becomes crucial for aiding the nearby burned city.

Nothing out of the ordinary happens here. It’s a quiet, safe place, perfect for resting and preparing for the journey ahead.

[h3]Ashes of Seashell Bay – Burned Harbor[/h3]

[i]"Used to be a fine port, it was... now is’s just smoke, screams, and beggin’ eyes. Best bring more than pity, mate." — First Mate Grigory, witness to the burning[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/fd46cd005533346a578ef4e3db4f1b795ad26735.jpg[/img]

Seashell Bay Harbor is a ruined city, recently devastated by an attack from the Trade Company. Its people are struggling to survive and have little to offer, except a desperate need for resources and support.

[h3]The Storm’s Refuge – Atoll Fort[/h3]

[i]"Ye don’t stroll into that atoll, lad – not unless ye fancy dancin’ cannonballs with Captain Storm hisself!" — Captain Rakes, survivor of the Outer Fort Clash[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/98cd51cf19a4d4b98ffbb9f4370204f43d55cfba.jpg[/img]

At the heart of a remote atoll lies a small settlement guarded by a powerful fort. It’s a Trade Company-controlled area located on the edge of their territory and home to the infamous Captain Otto, also known as “The Storm.”

Reaching this place is no easy task — you must first deal with the fort. A key moment involves ambushing a supply convoy to weaken its defenses. 

[h3]The Totem Watchers – Seeker Research Camp[/h3]

[i]"They say they study totems... but I swear by me compass, those Seeker rats got darker plans than they let on." — Black-eye Jack, ex-cultist turned smuggler[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/04f3da5c19883ec996e9b7b647de3ea7f9cf7d32.jpg[/img]

On one of the islands, a camp of strangers studying a mysterious totem linked to the local tribes can be found. These outsiders call themselves the “Seekers of Order” and seem to be engaged in odd rituals and research.

[h3]Black Rocks Haven – Pirate Hideout[/h3]

[i]"Now this be a place fer real sailors—no law, no questions, just rum, powder, an’ coin changin’ hands." — Joe, quartermaster and fence[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/149a338bc9d48ed296f35e42443cb06d6f4c694d.jpg[/img]

Hidden among sharp coastal rocks is a small pirate hideout. It's one of the few places where players can resupply deep within Trade Company territory.

This hideout serves as a launch point for raids against fishing villages and enemy camps. It’s also a black market hub where looted goods — especially from Seeker camps — can be sold. Despite its location in hostile lands, the hideout itself remains safe and free from immediate threats.

[h3]Flames of Disorder – Burning Seeker Camp[/h3]

[i]"I’ve sailed through ghost waters an’ stared down storms, but I swear on Blackbeard’s beard—I ain’t stayin’ the night in that camp." — Old Man Hank, last seen leavin’ without his boots[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/e37300a3323cd7c2a696730ac3c3fae8e2fda85f.jpg[/img]

Hidden on the edge of archipelago island, Whispershade Hollow is a quiet, unsettling encampment. The people here are... strange. They speak in riddles, move in silence, and seem to worship something they never name aloud. Whether they’re mystics, fanatics, or madmen is anyone’s guess — but none of them seem entirely sane.

There are whispers of secret rituals, strange symbols carved into trees, and a presence in the air that chills even the boldest pirate to the bone. 

[h3]Deadman’s Nook – Pirate Hideout in Company Lands[/h3]

[i]"Only a madman or a true pirate sets up shop this deep in Company waters... lucky fer us, I be both."  — Scarface Jim, founder of the Nook[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/47371e5da302ac4e592a14029ebd6f826f03f673.jpg[/img]

Deadman’s Nook is a hidden pirate outpost tucked right into the heart of Trade Company territory. It’s a rough, quiet place, carved out of desperation and defiance. The pirates here keep their heads low and blades ready—every supply run could be the last.

Despite the risk, it’s one of the few places where players can resupply behind enemy lines. Black market deals, whispered plans, and forbidden maps often pass through this little outpost—if you know who to talk to.

[h3]Shark Bay Harbor – Trade Company controlled Port[/h3]

[i]"They call it order. I call it chains in velvet gloves." — Mistress Vyra, pirate with unfinished business[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f673efa348ddd40be1ae26694d9ccde6ccc41222.jpg[/img]

Shark Bay Harbor is a bustling Trade Company port, strictly controlled and heavily patrolled. Outsiders are met with suspicion, and pirates even more so. The city is a fortress of “law” and profit for the Trading Company itself — but the cracks are starting to show.

While it begins as a hostile zone, some choices and actions may slowly turn the tides. Influence can be gained. Loyalties can be shaken. Perhaps even this Company stronghold can be turned to your advantage… for a price.

[h3]Ironhold Bastion – Fortress of Samuel “Iron Hand”[/h3]

[i]"I once tried to sail past Ironhold at night... the stars vanished from the cannon smoke. I ain’t goin’ back." — Blind Pete, survivor of the Night Barrage[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f2b53c0e2b9ce0b07874e15b6cc9dc6d6fe5ed00.jpg[/img]

Ironhold Bastion is the crown jewel of the Trade Company’s military might—a fortified island citadel, guarded by cannons, sea mines, and the flagship frigate of the infamous Samuel "Iron Hand", the Company’s ruthless leader.

Approaching this place without a plan is madness. The bastion is not just a stronghold—it’s a symbol. Taking it means striking at the very heart of the Company’s power. It won’t be easy, and it won’t be quiet… but it might just be legendary.

That’s all we’ve prepared for you today. We hope you enjoyed it, and we’d love to hear what you think in the comments below!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - Playtests
notes.notes:
Ahoy, pirates!

We’ve had an incredible journey with all of you during these early playtests of Pirate Commander. We want to give a heartfelt thanks for your time, your feedback, and your dedication. It’s been an amazing experience to share our work-in-progress with such a passionate and engaged community. From detailed survey responses to lively discussions on Discord, every piece of input has helped us uncover new ideas and shape the future of the game.

We’re now taking all of your insights into account as we refine and improve gameplay mechanics, balance, and overall design. Our goal is to create a truly immersive pirate adventure—one that captures the thrill of the open seas, the excitement of naval battles, and the challenge of managing a fearless crew.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/cfd6e849cfc2508324a6b85d252b1137cb617fa5.jpg[/img]

Remember, this playtest version will remain accessible until March 17 for those who already have access. If you haven’t jumped aboard yet, there’s still time to sign up. We may open another testing round in the future once we’ve incorporated your feedback and further polished the experience.

Thank you again for your enthusiasm, your patience, and your spirit of adventure. We look forward to sharing more updates soon. Until then, keep your sails trimmed and your compasses steady, and may the winds always favor your journey!



DevTeam Pirate Commander

⚓ Remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #11
notes.notes:
Ahoy!
Finally, we can show you a glimpse of what we’ve been working on over the past few weeks. What would a pirate game be without the most exciting way to fight and plunder enemy ships? Of course, we’re talking about boarding...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/8f06e6670b247d50cc2f7534480745ef0bc112fe.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/3dd0538ffdfcccbdb46d55ec3a265780a2dac4a3.jpg[/img]

Not only will you be able to destroy enemy ships from a distance, but with a bit of luck, you’ll also get close enough to board their vessel. This way, you can not only earn more rewards but also save on potentially expensive repairs to your own ship!

But before you can engage in boarding, you need to prepare properly. The first step is to go to the ship management screen and select the appropriate menu option to assign sailors for combat. In this window, you can place sailors in specific locations on the deck, allowing you, as the captain, to decide where each crew member will fight. The second part involves selecting equipment. The game offers three weapons: a saber, a pistol, and a musket. We’ll share more about these weapons and how they impact combat in future posts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/785de923018f50ddefd6615283fba0c307f5f9bc.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/3cf98fed7a334e9830651c34691abfbeb228fcfd.jpg[/img]

It’s worth mentioning that each weapon icon in the armory not only represents the weapon itself but also the ammunition available for it. Hence, deploying a sailor with a specific weapon will consume one unit of the corresponding resource.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/6621724d732caca9faa9cad2d3bdd1307ee6a196.jpg[/img]

Once your crew is armed, it’s time to find a potential opponent. Ideally, your target should be slightly weaker than you to ensure the rewards are worth the fight without risking defeat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/1fa7692e5e53cc8ff53ed48fc7f44b344c924aae.jpg[/img]

After selecting your target, it’s time to battle. You’ll begin with ranged combat, during which you can approach the enemy ship and execute a boarding maneuver once you’re close enough.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/000aaa2d3740bf77882f3aaa8ecd3de3fde144ff.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/2f323e04f815103cc62299aaca149c537f50bb6d.jpg[/img]

After a successful boarding maneuver, the fight transitions to melee combat. As you can see, the player’s sailors are positioned at the bottom of the screen, while the opponents are at the top. The arrangement of your sailors and their equipment reflects the choices you made in the arming window.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/e3e89435e024f9c6fc1a54e40080d4626b57a013.jpg[/img]

During the fight, the player can freely move the camera and rotate the view, making it easy to observe the battlefield during the skirmish.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/ddd2d7e977d27fd8e9b57c8f1db40bd6f363fa11.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/ec245e7e400319b139628d8828ab5ea7f31484ef.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/13402b4adea88b50857b441a4bc1359501000752.jpg[/img]

That’s all we have prepared for you today. In the coming weeks, we’ll delve deeper into the combat system and share more details about the mechanics of fighting. Let us know what you think!

Remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #10
notes.notes:
Ahoy!
In today's DevLog, we will provide you with information about crew management on the ship. This is one of the most important tasks for any captain, as well-given orders and well-planned actions not only allow for optimal preparation for each battle but also ensure the economy of our ship is well taken care of.
Remember, what we’re showing is still a work in progress, so expect some elements of the interface to be further polished.

Upon entering the side view of the ship, the player will be able to access the crew assignment view. At the bottom of the screen, a panel with thumbnails of available sailors will be displayed. This panel will show the sailor's name and basic attributes, such as strength, dexterity, and perception.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/e28f05c02d4c7485362a38344528a34c573131d7.jpg[/img]

If we select a sailor, we will also see their full profile panel, including details like their experience level and how much more experience they need to reach the next level. Additionally, the selected sailor will be highlighted (making it easy to locate them on the ship), and their destination will be marked with a pulsating line.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/08bb8716112dbcd8b147b25bc34baa697f4f9249.jpg[/img]

Moreover, all built cabins in this view will display icons representing the possible interactions available in each cabin. For example, in the combat cabin, there are three positions for sailors: gunner, aimer, and loader.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/15eba54474803e4c1f4a987750bb21aae977ab73.jpg[/img]

This makes assigning sailors to the appropriate stations simpler and allows you to focus on preparing for battles. To make assignments easier, the system uses a drag-and-drop mechanic, allowing you to move sailors' portraits from the bottom panel to the slots in the cabins.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f6263dbc9f290186bdadb61a4bb20556f60d6d08.jpg[/img]

That’s all we wanted to show you today. Thank you for your continued support, and we’ll talk to you again soon!

Remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #9
notes.notes:
Ahoy Captains!

Today, we will give another glimpse of combat and ship management mechanics - cabin damage system.

During the combat, enemy ships can damage your ship sections and, therefore, take our guns out of action.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/18d3d1eea8f53949a9da00bbe30680de4cb617da.jpg[/img]

This is the immediate effect during combat, but the consequences of taking damage are more serious. When the combat is finished, we can go to the ship management view and take a look at the damage done during the battle to each cabin in the section.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/ba0fa7865c96b85740bfe69d43bbc0395922a17b.jpg[/img]

It is important to note that we lost the HP section during the combat, which summarizes the cabin's HP. When the combat is over, this damage is allocated to each cabin.
From the ship management view, we can see which cabin is damaged.

Take a look at the visualization of each damage threshold:
Cabins without damage
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/10511f10a6cc2c1ef5918f0f87a2e1b79b0f13b9.jpg[/img]
Cabins with minor damage
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/e0d9f6b72d2b6071bcfd2af344cc521008103d07.jpg[/img]
Cabins with moderate damage
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/9681c56cb51c9324f6b63e2b3ce34ca2ac7f89c2.jpg[/img]
Cabins with significant damage
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/5f60f23abd8234eaf9a1fc4835f18afb4316c916.jpg[/img]

Of course, based on the available resources, now is the time for you to decide which cabin to repair first. You can do this by spending repairing tools from your ship's hold.

Each repair tool restores 50 HP to the cabin. You can regain used tools in two possible ways:
buying them from workshops placed on the map, 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/40cab6badc6880264459aa4f3ceddb1441ec89ad.jpg[/img]
or by building shipwright cabins and sending skilled crew members there to craft new tools from wood and metal. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/d39a1c7bf0f1ec553fa0ba4d503a77d5366c8a0d.jpg[/img]

That's all that we have prepared for you today. Let us know your thoughts, and remember that fortune favors the bold!

Remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #8
notes.notes:
Ahoy Captains!

After some time, we are now getting back to you with an update about the mechanics we have been working on lately to improve the tactical aspect of range naval combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/0b8f1c0ebfcfe2aaa19098b6ae44e2fb4cbecba5.jpg[/img]

Let's delve into the heart of naval combat tactics-distance and maneuvers.

First, let's talk about distance. It's not just a number on your screen but a crucial factor in naval combat. It determines your chance of hitting and the damage you deal. Keep an eye on the distance indicator on the left side of your UI to know how far you are from the enemy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/1c92baefc8d7b71592c04b45406f7739232fdb03.jpg[/img]

The second element of tactic is performing special skills that we call maneuvers. The maneuvers are based on the captain's order, which tells the crew what to do and how to steer the ship. In this post, we will scratch the surface of this part, and we will discuss only four basic maneuvers:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/89babea0922effbf74d76dc6095acf6f90bda5b5.jpg[/img]

[b]Salvo![/b] - The captain motivates sailors to double their efforts when loading guns and firing. It allows you to fire all guns at once with only slightly reduced effectiveness

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/38520e883da102b00bf212764aedd5130d93ecf6.jpg[/img]

[b]Evasive Maneuver[/b] - A maneuver that causes the player to sail with a variable direction and speed. As a result, it is much more difficult for the enemy to hit the player's ship. Performing this maneuver also makes aiming slightly more difficult.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/367ba7f9ccba494a48a4ee2dd36fb7b62ed7ea4d.jpg[/img]

[b]Approach Maneuver[/b] - Approaching an enemy ship by a specified number of distance units.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/2638831159c38e3e167b183c6f881fc6878b2484.jpg[/img]

[b]Depart Maneuver[/b] - Moving away from an enemy ship by a specified number of units of distance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/ea2c6488a809c32068e040c64874f4c85ead63c2.jpg[/img]

Also, it is essential to add that each maneuver has a cooldown, and the cost is expressed in maneuver points (offensive, defensive, and utility). So, it is crucial for each captain to manage the available points appropriately and use them wisely, depending on the sea situation. We will discuss the maneuver points in more detail and how to get them in the upcoming posts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/8a8079b634aafbf743374f364abe041c736e36ae.jpg[/img]

Thank you for reading, and let us know what you think about Maneuvers.
 
Remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #7
notes.notes:
Ahoy Captains!
 
It is time to show you a little bit more about ranged combat with enemy ships. Therefore today we will show you some insights about the ship damage system.

As we have mentioned last time, the ship is divided into several sections:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/7188ae385e6c7e9ffa56a5d93f0be1395ed26a67.jpg[/img]

Each section has parameters associated with it, such as hit points, armor, difficulty of hitting, and some special properties. Additionally, each section may contain cabins that significantly affect the further course of the battle. For example, destroying an ammunition depot can lead to a dangerous ignition and fire, and destroying a section full of guns can significantly weaken the offensive power of the opponent.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/86aa444caf382c7cf7b126caef43c1708ce32129.jpg[/img]
 
Now let us show you how section damage progresses on different parts of the ship:

SAILS:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/fc0bb56c7d3f0ade9699790d0b4e3e7342cbd11c.jpg[/img]

DECK:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/6729baebe46d7f25ed9b53b59757cff5fe36503c.jpg[/img]

STERN:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/04a0442cef5bcbc2c283d2dcf45ffa15780a8866.jpg[/img]

MIDDLE DECK: 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/2d0319e6b7f6151e14e3ef09e3c655fa25cd7081.jpg[/img]

LOWER DECK:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/eb8ba6d32207471b390bc934cd24523f836ca308.jpg[/img]

PROW:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f86331de829a44c57428615e69422bfd1d7e6d80.jpg[/img]

In order to win the combat you must be faster than the opponent to destroy at least four of six sections of the enemy ship. If you manage to do that you will be rewarded with such a beautiful view of sinking enemy ship and of course the possibility of getting treasures floating on the water.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/v4VrZTE.gif[/img]

We hope you like this little introduction to the ship damage system, please let us know what you think. 


Remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #6
notes.notes:
Over the last few days, we have been working on one of the key elements of the game, which is sea battles. 

Today we are going to tell you a little bit about the direction we are heading in and our plans about combat in game, so you can give us some feedback. This article is just an initial part that shows only the fracture of the entire combat mechanic that we have in plans. More about it like maneuvers, sail management will come!

The battle begins in the exploration view where we can encounter other ships sailing  endless oceans and countless islands. It's hard to name the other ships hostile, after all, we are the pirates, so woe to everyone in our path!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f689f4f4d8348ebac9a645f9fe49c7add7c66419.jpg[/img]
After selecting an opponent and entering into range, the actual battle begins.

We play the fight from a slightly different view than during exploration. The initial battle view is presented below:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/cd211499a1a9bdc168864dd931308fb3e0c42ad4.jpg[/img]
The combat takes place in real-time. At the bottom of the screen, depending on how many cannon stations we have built, we have icons representing our cannons. Each cannon is characterized by several statistics and information about which crew members currently operate it. Both the type of gun and the crew operating it affect accuracy, fire frequency, and damage dealt. A capable crew simply knows where to aim and where the weakest parts of the enemy ship are to cause the greatest damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/c8465d96fb98b0804bdfc3a70ea52373c981140b.jpg[/img]
The first step in battle is to look at your opponent's ship sections. The type of ship will determine which combat tactics will be the most effective. In the combat view, we can look at its individual sections and analyze all kinds of modifiers related to them. Aiming it's not only about the difficulty of hitting or armor but also some additional information, such as knowing where the ammunition storage is located. Hitting ammo storage is an extremely tasty morsel that allows you to cause devastating damage or even cause a huge fire.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/c7b87f477b9a08dfba086a9ed357376727cab729.jpg[/img]
Then, after the inspection, we must decide which firing stations available in our arsenal will be best suited to attack which sections of the enemy ship. It is worth noting that potential losses on our side should be taken into account because the enemy will not wait for our actions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/d716397f4d0a0743519bbb858e706e12e9968780.jpg[/img]
After choosing a target, we must carefully observe whether our decisions have the desired effect and, if necessary, react quickly. Not all types of cannons are good for all types of enemy ship hulls (armored one etc.). Sometimes it's better to use weapons that deal less damage but with high armor penetration. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/40bcec8fc8b61aaabdf51886f13427ca1a39f300.jpg[/img]
Today's article covers only one aspect of the fight against enemy ships, and more specifically, it talks about how aiming with cannons will look like. In future posts, we will cover a little bit more about the maneuvers we can perform during battle, about distance, and other gameplay mechanics available during sea battles.

Thank you for following and we are waiting for your feedback!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #5
notes.notes:
Ahoy Pirate!
 
In the last devlog, we wrote about the so-called POIs (Point of Interest) that symbolise important gameplay elements in the exploration view. Today we want to tell you a little more about ports and sectors.
 
The game map itself is divided into sectors that the player will travel in. Each sector will have a specific Tier, and on this basis the player will be able to decide whether he wants to go there. The higher the tier, the game becomes more difficult and the more demanding the challenges are, but also the greater the reward. Below, you can see the boundaries of the different sectors.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/da514f4f7fa4f73a05604cb9674534d3e1f76f51.jpg[/img]

Within each sector, apart from the POIs presented in the previous post, the player will be able to visit ports and use their benefits. In the following, we will discuss the first batch of buildings that may appear in a given port. The number of functional buildings there are in a port can vary from sector to sector, and it is impossible to be sure until a given port is discovered.
 
Now let us get into details of the first set of port buildings.
 
Tavern
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/4bc547343711952aa944679bb911d69ea697efb9.jpg[/img]

The tavern is a building that we visit to look for new sailors who will join our crew for a certain fee and the promise of treasures. After reaching the port and selecting the Tavern, the player can choose one of the 3 available crew members. After a while, new sailors can be found in the Tavern, so be sure to visit it after a while.
 
Market
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/d87993c336f61237f806529f5fb73534dfd298e2.jpg[/img]

This is a building that allows you to trade with a given port. Each port buys and sells up to three different goods. It is worth checking the cost of raw materials in each port you visit because from time to time the needs of the city may change and thus the cost of purchase and sale can change significantly. A good captain always checks prices and can make a fortune by carefully planning the transport of raw materials from one place to another.
 
Shipyard
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/e229a54ca21f37bb251325b0d207ed763db8b8f4.jpg[/img]

During sea battles and boarding combat, the integrity of the ship can often be damaged. Then you need to dock at port and ask experienced shipwrights to repair it.
 
More information about ports and its buildings we will introduce a little bit later. Meanwhile, remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #4
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f93205bfbba7063b51815c830069850b909ca99a.jpg[/img]
Hello sailors!

The captain and his crew must travel through many distant lands on their way to wealth and glory. To survive the dangers lurking there, you will first need to prepare both the ship and the crew. To do this, you need to collect the necessary resources and properly build the ship, ensuring that you have enough gold for your crew pay and enough supply of cheering potion for sea wolves - rum.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/4ec8bc26fb93e29ad62a143bb516fb1b111b694a.jpg[/img]
There are several resources that you can gather in Pirate Commander during the exploration of the Archipelago. Some examples of them are as follows:
1. wood - the basic building material for both the ship and the cabins

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f2a59bd7b2e31b9ea8caa7d4c3488eef65a170f8.jpg[/img]
2. metal - is an essential raw material for creating metal elements of the ship, including cabins and weapons as well as tools to repair the ship

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/d3f317aa362fdfdb1fc0c1a57b6a546050fd0fe9.jpg[/img]
3. herbs - a raw material used by alchemists to brew healing potions necessary for each sea wolf to heal after the combat

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/308fa4a1f774243785c149116bdb23176e055315.jpg[/img]
4. gold - a resource obtained by completing tasks, robberies, selling goods, etc. Gold is a universal currency opening every path, so it allows you to buy other resources, pay your crew, and more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/9b4af640f69d606c18a85770729ccdb027150561.jpg[/img]
In order to find introduced resources there are several ways to do so. 

The first one is the exploration of the map in the search of raw material stockpiles. Unfortunately, this method of increasing the number of resources is not the best one. Although it offers a free and easy way to fill in your warehouses, it is just a one-time use only. Once the resource stockpile is collected, it is no longer available.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/1d7e8f209d1890b3235abeca7f42d0de19b02387.jpg[/img]
The second way to obtain resources (more reliable) is to find the merchants scattered over the archipelago. Merchants are able to sell you the produced raw material for a certain amount of gold. It is worth noting that they only have a limited amount of resources to sell at once, but they are replenished from time to time. It is, therefore, worth planning your trip first to visit several of them during a single voyage from one port to another.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/a8179a2f6e79a1519fe737284281b692052ab678.jpg[/img]

There will be more options for you to collect needed resources like performing quests, visiting distant ports, and of course, plundering other ships but we will talk about them more in future Dev Logs. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/0297801fdefcdecd75f1ffe2b356c9da2983b434.jpg[/img]
Stay tuned for more news from Pirate Commander development in the upcoming weeks. 

Fair winds and following seas! 



Also remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #3
notes.notes:
Hello sailors!

Everyone knows that a pirate captain's home is her/his ship, which is why everyone takes care of it as if it were their most precious treasure.

In Pirate Commander it will be no different. To make everyone feel at home on their ship, we want to give players the opportunity to make their own decisions about how your ship is built. Therefore, the entire ship has been divided into slots in which the player chooses what to build. As a result it is up to you what will be available on your ship, and where.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/2ef58c08ca39f91ba0433500b292efe53220013f.jpg[/img]
This is particularly important because, during a naval battle, we do not want the bullets to hit our ammunition stockpile. Not only will we lose cannonballs, but we will get even more damage because of the extra explosion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/7658770c922797d3a73a9570d29cdf72bf85fe31.jpg[/img]
Now let us give you some examples of what you will be able to build.

The first type of cabins you can build are warehouses. This is where your crew will store treasures, raw materials, water, and weapons necessary for combat.

The standard warehouse is used to store raw materials such as raw meat, rum barrels, medicines, and wood or metal for repairing damaged ship components.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/523c8539a8d3510dfa3ea0bbb8bf046a007bd802.jpg[/img]
The armory is a room where small arms, flintlock pistols, rifles, and other items important in combat are stored. After all, no one goes to a canteen to drink rum in full gear!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/99f44e6af2a7314909ec6fcbc2b46710a5ca6b86.jpg[/img]
The last type of warehouse is the ammunition stockpile. This is where everything related to long range combat is stored like: cannonballs, gunpowder, blunderbuss ammunition, and ballista bolts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/df1f8f4a45b050e834a227e180a00f3893796fb6.jpg[/img]
The second type of cabins we wanted to tell you about are production cabins. Thanks to them, instead of buying expensive items in ports, you will be able to find raw materials during the exploration and craft the necessary items by your own crewmembers. Some examples of craftable items are: repair tools for hull, meals for crew, or medicines to restore hp of sailors.

The first example of a production cabin is a shipwright. Her/His task is to ensure that there are never a lack of materials to repair the ship, even after the hardest battle. For this purpose, he uses wood and metal from the ship's warehouses and produces ship repair kits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f0e5999ee125158a4cb8b855ef53e55898efae85.jpg[/img]
The second production cabin is the cook, who may seem to have no significant role, but is actually crucial to maintaining high crew morale. A well-fed crew, with full bellies after a good fight, is more willing to fight for their captain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/bcafcb7e3189ac7c6113309770420b8d06624d24.jpg[/img]
The last cabin is the alchemist. There is no fight to make sure everyone gets out unscathed, and sometimes broken limbs or deathly rot are the smallest health problems that torment your crew. Fortunately, a good alchemist in her/his cabin is able to create healing potions that can do miracles. These potions are able to make your crewmates get back on their feet even if they are already half-way in the afterlife.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/b6cda04490c449882086e79bbd2d724aa62d63de.jpg[/img]
To sum up, today we showed you a small sneak peek of what you will be able to build on your ship. We started with the cabins responsible for the economy, and in one of the next posts we will reveal a bit more of the ship's combat options. So remember to follow us on Steam and let the wind blow in your sails!

Also remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #2
notes.notes:
Aye Sailors!

Some time has passed since our last post, so we are coming back to you with a bunch of new information about the progress of our work.
Today we will discuss one of the most important Pirate Commander game perspectives called "Navigation View". An Navigation view is a view where you can observe the game from the isometric perspective. Thanks to that you are able to plan your next actions based on the surroundings, and explore the unknown parts of the world map!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/CVoA3iD.gif[/img]

In this view, your task as the captain would be to explore subsequent sectors (one example is shown below) of the world, where numerous dangers and treasures await you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/5f5cd8d4a1dedac51a14eb8765dfb9a9e15f850e.jpg[/img]

While exploring the world of Pirate Commander, you will look for hidden treasures or search through the old, forgotten shipwrecks. Searching for them will often turn out to be just a waste of time, but sometimes in their storage, you will discover forgotten cargo. Among the crates with moldy food and stale rum, you will find a mysterious artifact that you have been talking about to your mates! Becoming the owner of a such precious treasure is the key to making a fortune.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/c3435cd2e816c365f74eb6d82cc1c60d3917d5c3.jpg[/img]

As Captain, you will navigate your beloved ship to the unknown to discover new lands. People there can offer rare goods and if you maintain good relations, they will be happy to trade with you. In port settlements, you can also count on recruiting new crew members, improving the ship, or taking on numerous quests. This quest will not be limited to escorting the ship or transporting cargo, but we will tell you more about this on another occasion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/7c1bdccf9fb2607f3825807adce2d3f00d0d3ee0.jpg[/img]

The bravest and most persistent captains will even be able to sail to mysterious northern lands. The severe weather conditions in these lands, low temperatures, and treacherous icebergs effectively deter others, but not you! If you prepare properly, you will have the chance to be one of the first explorers of these lands, meet their mysterious inhabitants, and mark new sea routes!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/01766d11f5d37c5fa2ae6f1084774f6425f82ced.jpg[/img]

So, that is all we have prepared for you today! We hope you like this short introduction to exploration in Pirate Commander. Remember, this is only the beginning. We'll talk more about the game and its mechanics in the coming weeks!

Also remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #1
notes.notes:
Aye Sailors!

It's time for us to share some news about Pirate Commander! First of all thank you for wishlisting and following our steam page! Thanks to that we have a huge motivation to share our works and keep informing you all about our progress. In this first dev log we will tell you a general introduction to the game, but we plan to share news on a monthly basis so stay tuned for a more detailed description of all mechanics that we plan to implement!.

Next, before we dive into game development progress let us tell you a little bit about ourselves. We are A2 Softworks, a dev team of passionate game developers with rpg and strategy game history. We believe that our past experience with joint forces of Rock Games S.A. as a publisher will result in creation of unique and enjoyable game experience for you. 

Let's introduce a little bit more about the game. Pirate Commander is a unique mixture of roguelike-like game with deep crew management and elements of RPG and tactical game. You are the captain of the marine ship, and it's up to you what you will do with it. Maybe you will become a pirate that all ports and cargo ships will be afraid of. Or you will be the one who will take care of safety and, despite adversity, will always help the weaker ones. The choice is yours.

Pirate Commander is designed around a few main ideas, which we will outline in this post. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/V8T8sFl.gif[/img]

[b]Crew-Management[/b]
Your key to success is to choose the right crew for the ship they are on. Whether it's a mighty galleon or a swift sloop, a well-matched crew, with an appropriate range of specializations will decide whether you'll be victorious. In addition to recruiting experienced sea wolves, you will have to maintain   high morale of your crew. Victories at sea and liters of rum in the canteen will help you achieve this.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/0d0a5e98c45a4f2df8b19d1dda2a47eae3aac4a1.jpg[/img]
[b]Ship customization[/b]
Pirate Commander will allow you to command various ships, but ship type alone is not everything. You need to think about how to optimally build (place) cabins on the ship. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/e6f8730585921a5713bcdaebf2831e706d6fbd85.jpg[/img]
Remember, it is not a good idea if your crew needs to run through the whole ship, looking for ammo every time they shoot a cannon. On the other hand, placing your ammo storage close to the water, makes it harder to hit. So, as you see, there are no easy choices.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/eec3de483333d8e0df596881552946ba770d3708.jpg[/img]
[b]Tactics[/b]
During combat, the captain must make decisions crucial to the outcome of the battle. You will need to choose the right sails to perform complex battle maneuvers during ranged combat, and sometimes prepare for close quarters combat on your or your opponent's deck. 
The way you build your ship and manage your crew can have a great impact on your tactical options. Some players may install many strong cannons, blunderbuss or mortars on their ship to enhance its range capabilities, others may prefer fast ships with strong melee oriented crew, designed to board enemies.

[b]RPG elements and Exploration[/b]
In Pirate Commander you will explore the mysterious Archipelago, where each island and port is an independent city state. This land is full of pirates out to rob any merchant ship passing by. Lately, there are more and more  rumors about ships disappearing without a trace, and coastal settlements struggling with a strange plague. In these dark times, the Trade Alliance seems to offer shelter, but is it really a trustworthy organization? In the game, you will decide which regions of the Archipelago to visit, and completing quests will allow you to discover its darkest secrets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/4a3448f85b760c911f958604ed4ae99134f131d5.jpg[/img]
We hope that the elements of the game we revealed interested you, let us know what you think! We will tell you more about each element of gameplay and mechanics in upcoming weeks! 

Also remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!
